fuente: Documentary catalog vNext-1.0R: keep semantics and content, 14 classes NOT 14 files

clases.nombre: Direction, business model, and strategic boundaries
elicitacion: Compare real opportunities accepted and rejected: what signals make an opportunity a fit or not?
What work could pay well but the company deliberately declines, and why?
What wins when price, capacity, reputation, quality, and time conflict?
What activity or combination of capabilities is hard to copy, and why?
What does the company want to build or stop doing in the coming periods, and what evidence would change that decision?
contenido_obligatorio: Verifiable identity: real business and offers actually delivered; distinguish aspiration from current activity
Value model: payer, user, buyer, job to be done, exchange, and billing mechanics
Chosen and unchosen segments, geographic scope, restrictions, and explicit trade-offs
Competitive differences backed by real activities, not aspirational adjectives
Time priorities, capabilities/milestones, selection criteria, and review rules
Critical assumptions, counter-evidence, progress indicators with sources, and decision owner
Strategy changes, reasons, effective dates, and formally approved decisions

encabezados: 00 Verifiable findings and degree of certainty
03 Jobs, frictions, and alternatives per episode
06 What we do NOT know and contrast experiments
elicitacion: Compare excellent and problematic customers: what signals appear before they hire?
Which question, behavior, or circumstance best reveals the job the customer is trying to get done?
Which objections are literal and which usually hide a different concern?
What promise or claim would the company never make even if it helped sell?
Which belief about customers has changed after real experiences?
contenido_obligatorio: Explicit distinction between buyer, approver, payer, and user
Situations / Jobs to Be Done reconstructed from concrete episodes
Evidence per segment, sample size and bias; no extrapolation
Obstacles, alternatives used, decision criteria, and purchase triggers
Channels where contact is observed and verifiable messages
Positioning: desired versus perceived associations; authorized/prohibited claims
Knowledge gaps, discovery questions, and refresh signal

encabezados: 01 Map of modalities and commercial state
02 Promise, scope, and exclusions per modality
03 Prices and conditions: authority and validity
04 Commercial path from opportunity to agreement
elicitacion: How does the company build a price when the work does not match a standard offer?
Which components, costs, conditions, or exclusions must never be omitted when quoting?
When is a flat price, breakdown, module, package, or custom quote appropriate?
Which commercial exception can each person authorize, and which needs another approval?
What signals indicate a proposal is not ready to send yet?
contenido_obligatorio: Map of real lines: sold, pilots, products in development, internal tools, discontinued
Promise and scope per modality, exclusions, conditions, and customer evidence
Commercial mechanism: origin, qualification, diagnosis, offer, approval, closing, and follow-up
Public/particular price definition, currency, taxes, discount, validity, and approver
Sales and separation tests: delivery, purchase, handover, tool use, and cancellation
Rules for messages, statements, and claims authorized by D02
Handling of exceptions, refunds, warranty, and handoff to operations

elicitacion: Reconstruct a real difficult job from confirmation to close: where were the critical decisions?
What early signal lets you anticipate that delivery may go wrong?
Which part can follow a checklist and which part requires expert judgment?
Which error is costly/hard to fix and which control prevents it?
What does «done» or «accepted» mean for the company in practice?
contenido_obligatorio: Entry promise, acceptance criteria, and sales handoff
Real delivery flow map with triggers, inputs, outputs, and exceptions
Owner per task and who decides, without invented titles
Critical quality points and minimum completion evidence
Dependencies on people, systems, materials, and suppliers
Escalations and variants per offer type
Proven learnings and approved changes to practice

encabezados: 00 Financial read with date and currency
06 Criteria and authority for money decisions
elicitacion: How does the expert estimate whether a job is worth it before all costs are locked?
Which costs or consumptions does someone unfamiliar with the business usually forget?
When can a big project be worse business than a small one?
What criteria are used for advances, discounts, credit, purchases, or extraordinary expenses?
Which figure or signal is looked at first when making an economic decision, and what limitations does it have?
contenido_obligatorio: Revenue mechanics: agreed price, invoiced, accrued, and collected, tracked separately
Variable/direct and fixed/shared costs with declared allocation rules
Unit economics per line or job: numerator, denominator, period, sources, and exceptions
Cash: reference balance, expected inflows/outflows, maturities, and scenarios
Policies for advances, credit, discounts, and economic authorization
Targets and thresholds with formulas, currency, taxes, and owner
Sensitivities and alerts; reconciliation between narrative and accounting system

encabezados: 02 Who decides what, under what limits
elicitacion: If the founder/owner is absent for several days, what keeps running and what actually stops?
Which decisions can only one specific person make today, and why?
Which task could be delegated if the expert criteria were made explicit?
What critical knowledge lives in one person's head, and how do you recognize someone has learned it?
What is the difference between executing a task and having authority to commit the company?
contenido_obligatorio: Existing people/capabilities and functions actually performed
Simple decision matrix: subject, who decides, who prepares, who acts, and limits
Commitments requiring approval and current delegations
Dependencies on tacit knowledge, access, and capacity
Realistic substitutions and continuity limits
Learning transfer and task-based onboarding
Gaps and improvement projects without presenting proposed roles as real

encabezados: 00 Exposures and commitments that matter today
elicitacion: Which real problem has caused the most harm, rework, lost money, or reputational risk?
Which dependency would stop the company from delivering if it failed tomorrow?
Which risk does the company accept deliberately, and which would it never accept?
Which control or backup is taken for granted but has never been tested end to end?
Which commitments, permits, or reviews require a contractual/professional source instead of internal judgment?
contenido_obligatorio: Material obligations and legal/documentary source without substituting a contract
Risk: event, cause, impact on customer/cash/continuity, reasoned probability or «not estimated»
Existing versus proposed controls, warning signals, and owner
Suppliers/systems/resources whose loss interrupts the offer
Sensitive data, classification, access, retention, and limits
Continuity: contingency measure, recovery, source, and test
Permits/licenses and questions requiring specialist validation by jurisdiction

clases.nombre: Living record for an individual offer
elicitacion: What must the buyer be able to understand without extra conversation in order to hire this offer?
Which part of the scope changes most, and which must never be left implicit?
How is this offer's price built or authorized, and what exceptions exist?
Which condition makes this offer unsuitable for a customer/case?
Which acceptance/support/warranty criteria actually apply?
contenido_obligatorio: Identity: name, product/service/package type, variants, and state
Problem/use circumstance and validated audience
Deliverables, quantities, specifications, exclusions, customer responsibilities
Price rules, taxes, currency, dates, and approver
Acceptance conditions, changes, warranties, or proven support
Capacity, requirements, risks, and operational dependency
Versions: validity, replacements, and communication to dependents

encabezados: 00 What it is for and when it applies
elicitacion: Ask the executor to reconstruct a real run and point out decisions that are not in the checklist.
What signal forces the process to stop?
Which exception requires judgment and who can authorize it?
What evidence shows the process finished correctly?
What typical mistake does a novice make by following only literal steps?
contenido_obligatorio: Trigger and applicability condition
Inputs, versions, permissions, and preconditions
Observed steps and decisions; distinguish mandatory procedure from recommendation
Real roles, approval limits, and escalation
Results/evidence, acceptance criteria, record storage
Exceptions, contingencies, and stop signals
Last test and change versus previous version

clases.nombre: Relationship record with an account or customer
encabezados: 06 Open items, risks, and next contact
elicitacion: What real role does each contact play (user, buyer, payer, approver)?
Which needs were expressed by the customer and which are internal interpretation?
Which specific promises or exceptions remain valid for this account?
What information must not be generalized to the market?
Which access/retention/privacy restriction changes how the relationship is kept?
contenido_obligatorio: Minimal business identity and pseudonym if applicable
Roles: buyer, payer, approver, user, contact, and source
Chronology of material interactions and current conditions
Needs expressed in context, NOT psychological diagnoses
Confirmed opportunity state, sales events, and contractual references
Privacy and retention restrictions
Next decisions and tasks with owner and date

elicitacion: What changed materially during the case, and why?
Which decisions/exceptions were unique to the case?
Which problem did the expert detect, and what signal made it visible?
Which observed outcome supports learning, and which interpretation is still a hypothesis?
What, if anything, should be promoted to common knowledge through a separate decision?
contenido_obligatorio: Initial situation and actors, relevant jurisdiction/permissions
Timeline: date, event, source, change, effect
Requested, proposed, accepted, delivered, invoiced, and collected, kept distinct
Decisions and exceptions bounded to the case
Outcome evidence, incidents, limitations, and sensitive accounts
Lessons: observed fact, interpretation, scope, and proposed action
References to sources and dependents; policy changes only by separate approval

elicitacion: Which obligations matter most operationally, and which exact source proves them?
Which interpretation depends on professional advice and must not be resolved by AI?
Which dates/conditions change the compliance state?
What modification or exception exists relative to the general agreement?
Which other documents/processes/cash are affected by this agreement?
contenido_obligatorio: Parties and object, jurisdiction and source of authority
Obligations, restrictions, consideration, and dates
Precedent conditions, approvals, milestones, and contemplated remedies
Amendments, renewals, terminations, and disputes
Compliance state based on evidence (not inferred)
Risks and restricted data; legal reading to be confirmed
Links to affected projects, figures, and owners

elicitacion: Which business capability is lost if the resource/system/supplier fails?
What is the master source of the current state, and what must not be duplicated?
Who can administer/change/replace this resource?
Which capacity limit or dependency is usually discovered too late?
Is recovery/replacement tested or only declared?
contenido_obligatorio: Resource identity and business function
Registration system: where to query the current state
Operational owner/administrator and permissions without secrets
Dependencies of processes/offers/services
Capacity limits, replacement, and continuity
Expiry, conditions, evidence location, and cost when material
Incident history, changes, and recovery tests

clases.nombre: Decision, experiment, or lesson with its own identity
elicitacion: What exact decision/hypothesis is being preserved, and what alternatives were considered?
What signal/evidence changed the view or picked an option?
What outcome would falsify the hypothesis or force revisiting the decision?
Which part is contextual learning and which part could become policy?
Which dependents must be reviewed if this decision changes?
contenido_obligatorio: Precise question/decision, alternatives, and assumptions
Who has authority, who decided, date, scope, and validity
Available evidence, contradictions, and limits
Experiment success/failure rule, measurement, and review date
Observed outcome versus interpretation and possible transfer
Content promoted to policy only after explicit approval
Effects on documents and communication to users
